title: Identify Your Goods
heading_path: Controlled and Prohibited Goods > 01 Identify Your Goods
content:
Before importing, identify:
- What the goods are
- How they are used
- Where they come from
- Who they are for
If unsure whether your good is controlled or prohibited,
always check before importing them.
Check if your goods are controlled or prohibited →

title: Controlled Goods
heading_path: Controlled and Prohibited Goods > 02 Controlled Goods
content:
Allowed to Import with Approval
Controlled goods are allowed, but only with approval from the relevant Competent Authority (CA).
Common examples include:
- Medicines and health products
- Food items
- Plants and animals
- Drones
- Telecommunications equipment
- Weapons and replicas
Approval must be obtained before import.

title: Prohibited Goods
heading_path: Controlled and Prohibited Goods > 03 Prohibited Goods
content:
Not Allowed to Import
Common examples include:
- Counterfeit goods
- Obscene publications
- Certain weapons and explosives
- Endangered wildlife products
- Items banned under Singapore Law
Do not import prohibited goods.

title: United Nations Security Council Sanctions
heading_path: Controlled and Prohibited Goods > 04 United Nations Security Council Sanctions
content:
Some goods, persons, or countries are subject to United Nations Security Council (UNSC) Sanctions.
These restrictions may apply even if goods are otherwise allowed.
Sanctions may cover:
- Specific goods
- Named individuals or entities
- Certain countries or regions
Importing sanctioned items is an offence.
Check UNSC sanctions →

title: Obtain Permit
heading_path: Controlled and Prohibited Goods > 05 Obtain Permit
content:
If Required
If your goods are controlled:
- Obtain relevant CA’s approval
- Prepare required trade documents
- Obtain import permit
Valid permits must be obtained prior to importation.
Apply for an import permit →

title: Clearance of Goods
heading_path: Controlled and Prohibited Goods > 06 Clearance of Goods
content:
When goods arrive:
- Declarations are checked
- Permits and approvals are verified
- Goods may be inspected
Consequences of non-compliance:
- Delays
- Seizure of goods
- Penalties or enforcement action
Prepare documents for clearance →

title: Common Questions from AskGov
heading_path: Controlled and Prohibited Goods > 07 Common Questions from AskGov
content:
Q1: How do I know if my goods are controlled or prohibited?
A1: Self-check using the HS/CA Product Code Checker.

Q2: Can I import first and apply for approval later?
A2: No. Valid permits (including CA’s approval) must be obtained prior to importation.

Q3: What happens if I import prohibited goods?
A3: Goods may be seized and enforcement action may be taken.

Q4: Do UN sanctions apply to businesses?
A4: Yes. All importers must comply with UNSC sanctions.
